claims.text: WHO/Europe's statement of 30 June 2026 reports that Spain's mortality monitoring system has already estimated more than 300 heat-associated excess deaths in just a few days, that emergency medical calls in France have risen by up to 50% in some cities, that London's ambulance service recorded its highest-ever number of life-threatening emergency calls in a single day, and that Italy reported 5 deaths in 24 hours during the heatwave.

Re-checked 9 August 2026: WHO/Europe's most recent news item (31 July 2026), 'Wildfire smoke: a frequently underestimated health risk', addresses smoke exposure rather than an updated heat-mortality figure; its 16 July 2026 statement 'Planning for a warmer world' (nearly 10,000 excess heat deaths across five countries this summer) remains the latest heat-mortality figure published.

A WHO/Europe statement dated 16 July 2026 ('Planning for a warmer world') states that 'data from just 5 countries shows nearly 10,000 excess deaths due to heat' this season, consistent with this record's current estimate of approximately 10,000 deaths, and separately notes that 'in the past 4 years alone, heat has claimed more than 200,000 lives' across the WHO European Region (a cumulative, multi-year figure, not specific to 2026). No later WHO/Europe statement with a revised 2026 regional total was found as of 10 August 2026.

Re-checked 11 August 2026 via direct fetch of who.int/europe/health-topics/heatwaves: the most recent linked news items are 31 July 2026 ('Wildfire smoke: a frequently underestimated health risk'), 16 July 2026 ('Planning for a warmer world'), 30 June 2026, and 11 June 2026; no item newer than 31 July exists, and the 16 July 2026 statement's figure of nearly 10,000 excess heat deaths across 5 countries remains the latest heat-mortality figure published.

Re-checked 12 August 2026: WHO/Europe's heatwaves health-topic page still lists no news item newer than 31 July 2026 (wildfire smoke); the 16 July 2026 statement 'Planning for a warmer world' (nearly 10,000 excess heat deaths across five countries) remains the latest heat-mortality figure and is unchanged.

Re-checked 13 August 2026: WHO/Europe's heatwaves and climate-crisis pages show no newer mortality figure or resolution statement since the 16 July 2026 item (~10,000 excess deaths across 5 countries this summer); ECDC's 29 July 2026 release addresses heat-driven infectious-disease risk, not an updated toll. Non-allowlisted weather reporting describes a further heat dome affecting Western/Central Europe in mid-August 2026, consistent with the heatwave not having subsided.

WHO/Europe's statement of 7 July 2026, titled 'Extreme heat: more deadly weeks may still lie ahead for the European Region', warns that the current heatwave risk to health remains active and that heat-health action plans save lives.

WHO/Europe's statement of 16 July 2026, "Planning for a warmer world": "This summer's toll is still being counted but, already, data from just 5 countries shows nearly 10,000 excess deaths due to heat." WHO Regional Director Dr Hans Henri P. Kluge: "In the past 4 years alone, heat has claimed more than 200,000 lives, while heat-related mortality has risen by 30% over the past 20 years."

Re-checked 1 August 2026: WHO/Europe's news archive shows no statement on the heatwave newer than the 16 July 2026 'Planning for a warmer world' item; that statement (nearly 10,000 excess deaths across 5 countries, 200,000+ heat deaths over 4 years in the Region) remains the freshest figure, with no closure or resolution statement issued.

Re-checked 2 August 2026: WHO/Europe's 16 July 2026 statement, "Planning for a warmer world," remains the latest; no newer WHO/Europe statement has been published as of 2 August 2026, and figures are unchanged.

Re-checked 5 August 2026: WHO/Europe's 16 July 2026 statement, "Planning for a warmer world," remains live and is still the most recent WHO/Europe statement on the 2026 heatwave; a targeted search for a newer WHO/Europe news item on heat found none published as of 5 August 2026, and the nearly 10,000 excess-deaths figure remains unchanged.

Re-confirmed by direct fetch on 6 August 2026: WHO/Europe's 16 July 2026 statement 'Planning for a warmer world' remains the latest, with the quoted figure ('data from just 5 countries shows nearly 10,000 excess deaths due to heat') unchanged and the situation described as ongoing ('This summer's toll is still being counted'). No newer WHO/Europe statement specific to heatwave excess-death figures has been published.

Re-checked 7 August 2026 via direct fetch of who.int/europe: WHO/Europe's 16 July 2026 statement 'Planning for a warmer world' remains the latest, still citing nearly 10,000 excess heat deaths across 5 countries this summer and more than 200,000 heat-related deaths across the WHO European Region over the past 4 years; no newer WHO/Europe statement on the 2026 heatwave has been published.

Re-checked 8 August 2026: WHO/Europe's news archive and heatwaves health-topic page show no item newer than the 16 July 2026 'Planning for a warmer world' piece already cited (nearly 10,000 excess heat deaths across 5 countries); no newer WHO/Europe heat-mortality figure has been published.

description: A record-breaking series of heatwaves has gripped Western and Southern Europe since around 21 June 2026, straining health systems and emergency services across France, Spain, Belgium, the Netherlands, Italy and the UK. WHO/Europe issued successive public statements describing rising heat-associated mortality; its 16 July 2026 statement reported that data from just five countries already showed nearly 10,000 excess deaths from heat this summer, describing the season as a preview of a warmer future. As of 5 August 2026, no newer WHO/Europe statement has been published and no source has declared the heatwave over. Re-checked 8 August 2026: WHO/Europe's news archive and heatwaves health-topic page show no item newer than the 16 July 2026 'Planning for a warmer world' piece already cited (nearly 10,000 excess heat deaths across 5 countries); no newer WHO/Europe heat-mortality figure has been published. Re-checked 9 August 2026: WHO/Europe's most recent item (31 July 2026) addresses wildfire-smoke health risks, not an updated heat-mortality figure; its 16 July 2026 statement, 'Planning for a warmer world' (nearly 10,000 excess heat deaths across five countries), remains the latest heat-specific figure. Re-checked 10 August 2026: a WHO/Europe statement dated 16 July 2026 confirms 'nearly 10,000 excess deaths due to heat' from data covering just 5 countries, consistent with this record's approximately 10,000 estimate; no later WHO/Europe statement with a revised 2026 total was found. Re-checked 11 August 2026: WHO/Europe's heatwaves health-topic page lists no news item newer than the 31 July 2026 wildfire-smoke piece; the 16 July 2026 statement 'Planning for a warmer world' (nearly 10,000 excess heat deaths across five countries) remains the latest heat-mortality figure and is unchanged. Re-checked 12 August 2026: WHO/Europe's heatwaves health-topic page shows no item newer than 31 July 2026; the 16 July 2026 statement (nearly 10,000 excess heat deaths across 5 countries) remains the latest figure, unchanged. WHO/Europe's own framing ('toll is still being counted') and the absence of any closure statement support keeping this event ongoing. Re-checked 13 August 2026: WHO/Europe's heatwaves and climate-crisis pages show no newer mortality figure or resolution statement since the 16 July 2026 item (~10,000 excess deaths across 5 countries this summer); ECDC's 29 July 2026 release addresses heat-driven infectious-disease risk, not an updated toll. Non-allowlisted weather reporting describes a further heat dome affecting Western/Central Europe in mid-August 2026, consistent with the heatwave not having subsided.
